This is a source audit and artifact observation, not an exhaustive literature result or mathematical verification. Only the input, fresh workspace and ten authorized public caches were read. Running `python3 audit_sources.py > source-audit-output.txt 2>&1` successfully re-extracted all ten actual PDFs and reported every supplied hash check True. The saved 1201.0188 PDF is actual v1, SHA256 4c29d91987477baf9baa4dfdd0b901ae1cd8910746012fd6285ab9a90bbf3f3a. Its banner says v1, 30 Dec 2011, although its internal date reads 29 Oct 2018. Theorem A requires a complete discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, smooth projective algebraizable X, ample L, target mass c1(L)^n, and support on one SNC dual complex. Its internal date does not justify attributing a later-version statement to these bytes. Sections 2–7 construct the genuine bounded and finite-energy operator, energy and comparison without imposing target support. Algebraizability enters its Appendix A orthogonality argument. Proposition 8.2 states finite-energy uniqueness without orthogonality.

BFJ 1201.0187v2, SHA256 8b684713055b9147de0d3379ad925c58f031bafe10a77e769a2791cdaa128270, supplies normalized PSH compactness (Theorem 7.10), the envelope property and continuous envelopes (Theorems 7.11 and 8.3), and decreasing model regularization (Theorem B/8.7). Its setting is smooth projective geometry, ample polarization, and complete discrete residue-characteristic-zero fields. It does not require function-field algebraizability.

1805.01016v3, SHA256 51d02f75a65aa463f8e22393933f5ebef9036e322d720fc632f87759c2b71cb2, is Boucksom–Eriksson, Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. Theorem 8.4 supplies the genuine continuous mixed MA operator and continuity under uniform convergence. It is not a differently titled pluripotential paper or a general unbounded finite-energy equation theorem.

1801.08229v4, SHA256 8d5975337f4ac88a475929ea6a436ec4a15d08715d5582bc0ba0eb3e07152c52, establishes the arbitrary-support finite-energy theorem over an algebraically closed trivially valued field when X is smooth and characteristic zero, in arbitrary dimension. Its alternative positive-characteristic dimension-at-most-two statement is not used here.

2307.01697v1, SHA256 979daddbb2082320cd6bbe6f8522535e68b56d229317decd033c3101b9fdbaa1, supplies synthetic measure theory. Example 2.20 states test-function orthogonality for projective Berkovich spaces, using BE21 Theorem A and Boucksom–Gubler–Martin, Differentiability of relative volumes over an arbitrary non-Archimedean field, IMRN 2022 no. 8, 6214–6242, Lemma 3.2. This published background is invoked through the supplied source’s explicit assertion; no extra BGM PDF was supplied or fetched. Our smooth geometrically integral projective X is geometrically reduced, L is ample, and the semipositive model reference represents a class in Pos(X), satisfying the application domain. Theorem 1.26, Proposition 2.2, Theorem 2.23 and Lemma 2.25 provide the submean bound, coercivity and integral estimates. Theorem A/2.26 proves density and completeness on the measure side; Remark 2.14 sets aside the potential theory.

Actual PDF inspections are retained in source-extracts/synthetic-page25.png, bfj-v1-page27.png, bfj-v1-page28.png and bj-v4-page122.png. Synthetic (2.27) has absolute-value bars omitted by OCR. BFJ v1 Lemma 6.10’s actual printed statement contains a positive integral of −psi while its proof uses the negative integral of psi. The displayed statement alone cannot establish integrability; n3 proves the required bound directly.

Pille–Schneider 2209.04879v2 Remark 4.4 separates defining E1 over arbitrary fields from extending MA there. Field characteristic zero in that remark is not used to erase BFJ’s residue-characteristic restriction. Gubler–Rabinoff 2506.13548v2 explicitly leaves constructing MA outside its subject. Thuillier’s thesis supplies curve theory, without licensing a silent dimension-one restriction. Berkovich’s 1993 paper supplies analytic/cohomological background, not preservation of unbounded energy or MA under base change. The actual CLD 1204.6277v2 is the July 2025 revision; no application of its local-current theory to every global BFJ finite-energy target over arbitrary fields is established here.

Partial for original P16.6.
detailedSummary: Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 constructs the approximation-independent genuine finite-energy operator and solves the equation for every positive Radon target of raw mass V=(L^n) and finite dual energy. No skeletal-support or toric-invariance hypothesis occurs. The proof supplies compactness, envelopes, finite-energy differentiation, continuity of integration, comparison and injectivity. This established trivial-field result does not automatically transfer to discrete or arbitrary fields.
text:
Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and of characteristic zero; X/k smooth, connected, integral and projective, dimension n≥1 arbitrary; L ample; and the canonical trivial-field reference metric. Let V=(L^n)>0. Normalize intersection energy by E(0)=0 and E(u+c)=E(u)+c, and define E1={u psh:E(u)>−infinity}.

The exact target condition is positivity and Radon regularity, mu(Xan)=V, and raw dual energy sup_{a in model/FS tests}{V E(a)−integral a dmu}<infinity. For the entire probability nu=mu/V, this equals V Q(nu), where Q(nu)=sup_a{E(a)−integral a dnu}. No restriction of a target is renormalized. Constants make the raw supremum infinite at incorrect mass.

This theorem is already established in 1801.08229v4. Theorem 7.1 extends the genuine intersection pairing by majorants, uniquely and continuously along decreasing nets. Theorem 7.8 makes mixed pairings finite on E1. Theorem 7.18 tests this pairing against PL functions: positivity, mass V on constants, PL density and Riesz give a unique positive Radon MA measure. Proposition 7.19 verifies the model intersection formula and decreasing continuity. Therefore every decreasing model approximation gives the same genuine raw operator M(u), of mass V. No inverse measure construction is substituted.

Theorem 5.20 supplies the envelope property under the retained hypotheses; Corollary 5.21 gives compact normalized PSH; Lemma 5.17 gives continuous envelopes. Theorem 8.5/Corollary 8.6 gives differentiation through the envelope, with derivative integral f d(M(u)/V). Theorem 9.20 identifies finite Q with integrability of every E1 potential. Proposition 9.19 proves L1(nu) continuity on bounded-energy sets.

The printed proof of Theorem 12.8 normalizes a maximizing sequence for E−integral against nu, bounds its energy by (9.11), extracts a psh subnet using compactness, and uses Proposition 9.19 and energy upper semicontinuity to prove actual attainment. Corollary 9.12 identifies its maximizer with the genuine MA solution. Conversely, concavity and integrability against its own MA give Q(M(u)/V)=E(u)−integral u d(M(u)/V)<infinity. Thus the range is exactly the stated raw-mass-V finite-dual-energy measures. Theorems 7.40 and 7.44 give locality and comparison; Proposition 12.7 gives injectivity modulo constants; Theorem 12.9 concludes existence and uniqueness.

There is no support restriction, torus action or dimension-one assumption. The application is written in P16.6-argument.md and standalone P16.6-paper.tex/P16.6-paper.pdf; rerun `python3 build_artifacts.py`. This is a source-established mathematical theorem, not a finite computation. It remains partial for original P16.6 because its trivial-field hypotheses are not transported to other fields by unproved base change or measure completeness.

detailedSummary: The proof combines BFJ’s genuine operator, compactness and envelopes with the supplied synthetic orthogonality and integral estimates. It proves classical envelope orthogonality, extends quantitative test estimates to finite-energy potentials, establishes L1 continuity against arbitrary finite-energy targets, obtains actual variational attainment, and differentiates through unbounded envelopes to solve the genuine equation. The exact raw mass is V=(L^n), and the measure condition is sup_{a in D_theta}{V E_theta(a)−integral a dmu}<infinity. A printed BFJ v1 sign slip is bypassed by a direct integrability proof. No general-field compactness or envelope theorem is inferred, and no novelty claim is made.
text:
Retain K complete and nontrivially discretely valued with residue characteristic zero; X/K smooth, geometrically integral and projective, dimension n≥1 arbitrary; L ample; and a semipositive model reference with curvature theta. Field characteristic zero follows but does not replace the residue-characteristic hypothesis. No function-field algebraizability is imposed. Set V=(L^n)>0, M(u) the raw genuine MA and m(u)=M(u)/V. Model M is the intersection measure sum_E b_E(L_u|E)^n delta_{x_E}, of mass V. Use normalized energy E(u)=1/((n+1)V) sum_{j=0}^n integral u(theta+ddc u)^j theta^{n−j}, extended by decreasing majorants, and E1={psh u:E(u)>−infinity}.

The partial theorem is a bijection M:E1/R onto positive Radon measures mu with mu(Xan)=V and sup_{a in D_theta}{V E(a)−integral a dmu}<infinity. For the whole probability nu=mu/V, write Q(nu)=sup_a{E(a)−integral a dnu}. Constants force the raw mass. No toric, skeletal or dimension-one assumption occurs. This is a deduction from the source inputs in n1, not a claim that BFJ v1 Theorem A already stated it.

BFJ v1 Theorem 3.1 constructs the bounded mixed operator from intersections. Locality defines M(u)=lim_{t→infinity}1_{u>−t}M(u_t), where u_t=max(u,−t), as an increasing limit on Borel sets. For u≤0 in E1, the bounded energy difference formula gives E(u_{t/2})−E(u_t)≥t m(u_t){u≤−t}/[2(n+1)]. Decreasing energy continuity makes the discarded mass o(1/t), hence M(u) has raw mass V. Lemma 6.8 gives |integral f dm(u_t)−integral f dm(u)|≤2(n+1)|E(u)| ||f||/t. Proposition 6.9 gives decreasing continuity on E1, and model-test density proves approximation independence. To apply the source’s unit-volume convention, lambda=V^(−1/n), theta_tilde=lambda theta and u_tilde=lambda u satisfy M_tilde(lambda u)=M(u)/V and E_tilde(lambda u)=lambda E(u); cones and truncations correspond. Proposition 6.11 supplies genuine finite-energy locality and comparison, integral_{u<v}M(v)≤integral_{u<v}M(u). Proposition 8.2 supplies uniqueness modulo constants without orthogonality or target support.

The actual PDF statement of Lemma 6.10 has a sign slip. The needed integrability follows directly: for finite-energy u,v≤0 and w=(u_t+v_s)/2, positivity and bounded energy give E((u+v)/2)≤E(w)≤integral w dm(w)/(n+1)≤2^(−n−1) integral v_s dm(u_t)/(n+1)≤2^(−n−1) integral_{u>−t}v_s dm(u)/(n+1). Here m(w)≥2^(−n)m(u_t), w≤v_s/2, and locality permits discarding a nonpositive integral. Let s and then t increase through integers. Since m(u) is carried by {u finite}, sequential monotone convergence yields integral v dm(u)≥(n+1)2^(n+1)E((u+v)/2)>−infinity. Concavity makes the lower bound finite; constants handle unnormalized potentials.

Replace algebraizability-based orthogonality as follows. Synthetic Example 2.20/Definition 2.15 states lim_{a in D_theta,a<f} integral(f−a)dm(a)=0 for model f, using the directed pointwise order. BFJ 1201.0187v2 Theorem 8.3 makes P(f) continuous. Its decreasing model approximants converge uniformly by Dini; shifting them downward slightly makes them strictly below f. Consequently the entire increasing directed test net has supremum P(f) and converges uniformly. BE Theorem 8.4 passes genuine MA to the limit, yielding integral(f−P(f))dm(P(f))=0. Uniform model density, the 1-Lipschitz envelope property and continuous-MA convergence extend this to every continuous obstacle. This is precisely BFJ v1’s classical orthogonality hypothesis. Theorem 7.2/Corollary 7.3 now gives d/dt at zero E(P(u+tf))=integral f dm(u) for every u in E1 and continuous f, including unbounded u.

For arbitrary targets put m0=m(0), J(u)=integral u dm0−E(u), and r_nu(a)=Q(nu)−E(a)+integral a dnu. Synthetic (2.7) gives J(a)≤C_n(r_nu(a)+Q(nu)); its submean theorem gives sup u−integral u dm0≤T. Thus −E(u)≤J(u)+T on sup u=0. Finite Q implies integrability of every E1 potential against nu: decreasing model majorants a_alpha satisfy integral a_alpha dnu≥E(a_alpha)−Q, and the BFJ Radon/usc-net integration lemma passes this lower bound to u. Energy continuity proves Q=sup_{u in E1}(E(u)−integral u dnu). An unrestricted monotone-convergence theorem for arbitrary nets is not assumed.

Choose maximizing model tau_j, so r_nu(tau_j)→0 and J(tau_j) is bounded. Synthetic Lemma 2.25(2.27), with the second test potential zero, gives |integral a(dnu−dm(tau_j))|≤C_R r_nu(tau_j)^(1/2) uniformly for model a with bounded J. Its original right side contains J(a,0)^(2^(−n)), comparable to a bounded power of J(a). For a in E1, decreasing model majorants have converging energies and m0-integrals, hence converging J. Their nu-integrals and m(tau_j)-integrals converge as well. Therefore the estimate extends uniformly to all E1 potentials with bounded J.

If u_i→u in BFJ’s psh topology and J(u_i) is bounded, lower semicontinuity of J makes u finite energy. For fixed j, m(tau_j) has finite divisorial support, so its integrals of u_i converge to that of u. The uniform estimate, then j→infinity, proves convergence of the nu-integrals. For L1 convergence use w_i=max(u_i,u). Supremums and m0-integrals are bounded on a convergent psh net; energies of u_i are bounded below; monotonicity bounds energies of w_i below, hence J(w_i) is bounded. Divisorial evaluations give w_i→u. Apply integral convergence to both nets and |u_i−u|=2w_i−u_i−u. This proves L1(nu) convergence, including for the compactness subnet below.

Normalize a model maximizing sequence by subtracting its supremum. The bounds above control its J and energy. BFJ normalized-PSH compactness gives a subnet limit u; upper semicontinuity keeps u in E1. The proved L1 lemma yields E(u)−integral u dnu≥limsup(E(u_i)−integral u_i dnu)=Q(nu), hence equality. This is actual attainment. For continuous f, v_t=P(u+tf) lies in E1 because it dominates u−|t| ||f||, and remains below its usc obstacle. Maximality gives E(v_t)−E(u)≤integral(v_t−u)dnu≤t integral f dnu. Divide for both signs of t and use the finite-energy envelope derivative. Equality on all continuous tests gives m(u)=nu, therefore the genuine raw equation M(u)=mu.

Conversely, full mass, concavity and segment differentiation imply Q(m(u))=E(u)−integral u dm(u)<infinity; the directly proved integrability makes this finite, and decreasing approximation gives equality at the supremum. Thus the raw range is exact. Comparison and source Proposition 8.2 give uniqueness modulo constants. For a bounded model reference change theta'=theta+ddc h, transformed decreasing approximants prove M_theta'(u−h)=M_theta(u), E_theta'(u−h)=E_theta(u)−E_theta(h), and Q_theta'(nu)=Q_theta(nu)+integral h dnu−E_theta(h). Energy finiteness and the equation are reference-independent.

The dual condition is also equivalent here to E1⊂L1(nu). For the converse, integrability forces a uniform bound on −integral a dnu for normalized model tests J(a)≤1. Otherwise tests with integrals ≤−2^j give a decreasing convex series sum 2^(−j)a_j of energy ≥−(1+T), hence an E1 limit with integral minus infinity, a contradiction. Synthetic J(ta)≤C_n t^2J(a) then bounds −integral a dnu by A(1+sqrt(C_nJ(a))). Since E(a)≤−J(a), the dual supremum is finite.

It remains partial for original P16.6: compactness and the continuous-envelope passages used here have not been supplied or proved over general nondiscrete fields.
